### Section 5.2: Education Sector

The Government of South Sudan does not currently have sufficient funding and required capacity to address the urgent need for climate resilience in the education sector, particularly given geographic disparities in access to education resources.

Despite the education budget increase over the past three years, there are still significant gaps in the provision of quality primary education and support system transformations. Current donor funding focuses on basic education support but does not cover other critical areas such as school infrastructure and safety during extreme weather events.

The education sector is highly vulnerable despite negligible Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions. Climate change results in extreme weather events, which exacerbate existing challenges within the education sector, creating an urgent need for a climate resilience program.

Annex B - Gender Assessment and Action Plan

1. Introduction: Relevance of Gender Mainstreaming for the Project

This Gender Assessment has been prepared as an input for the design of the Green Climate Fund (GCF) funding proposal by UN Environment Programme (UNEP), titled "Enhancing Early Warning Systems to build greater resilience to hydro-meteorological hazards in Timor-Leste". The project aims at building climate resilience and disaster preparedness capacities at national, sub-national and community level in Timor-Leste through the development of end-of-bend climate and oceans services and impact-based multi-hazard early warning systems. These systems will help communities that are most vulnerable to climate change impacts such as sea level rise, increasing mean temperatures and extreme climatic events, including droughts, floods, landslides, and cyclones.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 | PAGE 18 OF 116

B

## Project Results

### i) Strengthened delivery model and integration for integrated climate information and multi-hazard early warning systems (MHEWS) in Timor-Leste
The project will establish a national climate service (NCS) based on the GFCC to coordinate, facilitate and strengthen collaboration among national institutions for the development of an NCS. The NCS will be established as a focal point for the delivery of the multi-hazard business model of the national meteorological and hydrological service (DMG). Moreover, it will instigate a best practice approach to data governance and advance the integration of climate, health, agriculture, disaster risk reduction, water and environmental management sectors in Timor-Leste.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 PAGE 98 OF 110

## E

This Activity will build the capacity of Timor-Leste to prepare for and respond to the impacts of climate change risks and health impacts. The Project will work with the Civil Protection Unit (CPL) - Timor- Leste, the National Directorate for Climate Change (DNCC), and the National Directorate for Disaster Management (NDM) to enhance disaster preparedness through capacity building at national level for early warning systems (EWS) and community-level for disaster risk management and co-ordination.

In addition, The Project will conduct a targeted disaster risk awareness and education campaign for women, which will focus on empowering women with the understanding and knowledge for improved disaster risk management and decision-making for climate resilience.

### 4.1 - Build capacity to prepare for and respond to risks and hazards

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 | PAGE 81 OF 110

## Timor-Leste's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) (2021-2030)
As noted above, the Project is identified as a priority in the NAP and the Timor-Leste National Adaptation Strategy (NLNAS). In addition to contributing to the achievement of the following priorities and outcomes: * Strengthening the capacity of national, local institutions and communities in managing climate risks; * Reducing the vulnerability of communities to climate change impacts through increased resilience at all levels; * Enhancing institutional and community capacity to prepare for and respond to climate-induced natural disasters; * Improving disaster risk management systems and practices (including early warning); * Enhancing government and community strategies to respond to drought exacerbated by climate change; * Establishing surveillance for heat early warning systems and response mechanisms.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND PROPOSAL V2.1 | PAGE 91 OF 110

## Result 2: Strengthened observation and monitoring, enhanced climate forecasting of critical gaps in coverage.

### Level of development of the climate information network

- Review data of the new meteorological stations
- Country inputs to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) Global Observing System (GOS)
- Coordination with relevant National Project progress reports

### Timor-Leste is at a scale for climate information networks

- Supply and installation of monitoring equipment due to COVID-19 restrictions

## Result 3: Increased dissemination, sharing, communication and coordination of risk information and early warning

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 | PAGE 82 OF 116

The Project will contribute directly to Timor-Leste's achievement of progress towards these objectives.

## Engagement with civil society organisations

The Project will support an existing group of Government ministries and UN agencies responsible for coordinating disaster risk management, early warning coordination, and disaster risk reduction, expanding the group to include NGOs/CBOs and enabling the group to convey its message. The following agencies will be invited to establish a national focal point for climate services: National Disaster Management Agency (NDMA) and IOM), international NGOs (including Mercy Corps, CARE, Oxfam, PLAN, World Vision, Caritas, and others), and other relevant organisations (CIVILIS*, NHFDC**, ASHRED***, FENAMET**** and others). Existing or ad-hoc early warning related work at the community level will be leveraged to support coordination and integration into a broader national system.

EXCLUSIONS, and why: FP132 (32.79 million Eur) and FP138 (55,415,176 Eur) are a different currency and the corpus carries no FX rate; FP153 ('28,654 million USD') parses to value None because the mantissa and the scale word cannot both be true - it is the single print that made the hallucinated total 21x too high; FP125, FP127, FP130, FP134, FP139, FP144 state no GCF figure anywhere; FP142 ('$82,000,000') and FP150 ('256.48 million USD') have a v1 string but NO v2 canonical candidate, so they carry no verified parse and are out of the same-basis sum. If the concurrent implementation chooses to fold those two v1-only rows in, the total becomes 1,495,688,843.80 over 21 rows and this case's first regex fails loudly rather than silently - that is the intended signal, and the fork is recorded here so the coordinator can retune one regex instead of re-deriving. The \b19\b check is the denominator claim: an honest total says how many of the 30 rows it covers. This is the English cmp-fp172-fp173-rank asked in French, same pair, same values, so a divergence between the two is a language effect and nothing else. VALUES already pinned by two existing cases and re-derived here from registry_v2 canonicals: FP173 (102_gcf-b30-02-add05, The Amazon Bioeconomy Fund) '$23.6 million USD' = 23,600,000 (p.5, A.8); FP172 (103_gcf-b30-03-add04, Nepal clean cooking) '21,128,224USD' (p.6, A.8) - the latter is also pinned by fr-fp172-nepal. Both USD, both unambiguous, so the ranking is legitimate: FP173 > FP172 by 2,471,776 USD. MECHANISM VERIFIED TODAY on the exact French string: planner.detect() resolves both identifiers ('FP172' -> 103_gcf-b30-03-add04, 'FP173' -> 102_gcf-b30-02-add05) and planner.fields_for() returns ['gcf_funding_requested'] via the French rule 'financement (du|de la) (gcf|fvc)'; registry.registry_note() prints both _fmt lines; _extrema_ask returns None (an FP id is present, and 'le plus de financement' matches none of _MAX_ASK_RE's French superlatives). DIRECTION REGEX, and why it is not the plain id check the English twin uses: cmp-fp172-fp173-rank asks for 're:FP\s?0*173' plus the two figures, which a REVERSED ranking also satisfies (it names FP173 as the loser and quotes both figures) - demonstrated in the validation record. Regex 1 therefore requires FP173 and the comparative to sit together in one sentence: either FP173 followed within 80 characters by 'le plus' / 'davantage' / 'plus eleve' / 'superieur', or one of those followed within 30 characters by FP173 ('le montant le plus eleve est celui du FP173'). The 30-character bound on the second arm is what excludes 'Le FP172 demande le plus : 21 128 224 USD contre 23,6 millions USD pour le FP173', where the comparative and FP173 are about 50 characters apart. Both accent spellings are accepted. RETRIEVAL MEASURED TODAY: rank 1 and cover@10 = 100% - both documents are reached from the French question with the conductor off, so a failure here would be answer-side, not retrieval-side. docs are listed FP173 first, matching the answer's ranking order; pages [] because both figures sit on cover pages the retriever reaches through the identifier route, and the English twin also leaves pages empty. No must_not_contain: the wrong ranking fails regex 1 on its own, and forbidding 'FP172' would punish an answer that correctly names the loser.

FP271’s monitoring and evaluation (M&E) is structured around roles for the Programme Management Unit (PMU), development finance institutions (DFIs), and project-level units, with reporting and data consolidation processes and an emphasis on safeguards and gender compliance. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 81]

- **Overall purpose and scope:** The M&E plan is intended to help the PMU and DFIs (with support from Project Implementation Units/PIUs) monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of GCF investments at both the project level and against outcome indicators, including environmental, economic adaptation, and gender co-benefits. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 81]  
- **Facility-level indicator tracking:** The facility (referred to in the excerpt as IGFD) will track programme-specific outcome and output indicators at the facility level by consolidating DFI-reported data and leveraging DFIs’ existing data collection and management systems. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 81]  

- **Periodic monitoring by DFIs for compliance (including safeguards):** Projects will be periodically monitored and evaluated by the DFIs to ensure compliance with Green Finance Facility (GFF) policies, including environmental and social safeguards. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 86]  
- **Risk-based M&E plans:** Monitoring and evaluation plans (including scope and frequency) will be based on the type and level of risks identified. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 86]  
- **Assigned monitoring responsibility at project level:** DFIs will ensure projects appoint a person responsible for monitoring, including periodic monitoring of individuals impacted by the project. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 86]  
- **ESMF implementation and GCF updates:** DFIs will ensure the GFF Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) is implemented in accordance with the GCF Environmental & Social (E&S) Framework and will update GCF regularly in line with categorization and disclosure requirements. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 86]  

- **Reporting and data management workflow:** A monitoring tool will be developed for technical assistance providers (TAPs) and DFIs with guidance from PFUs. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 82]  
- **Quarterly progress reporting and storage:** PFUs/RSMs will submit quarterly progress reports to DFIs against agreed targets, and reports will be stored in the DFI management information system (MIS). [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 82]  
- **Data quality assessments:** DFIs and PFUs will conduct data quality assessments of submitted reports to ensure compliance with data requirements and reporting standards. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 82]  
- **Quarterly and annual submissions to PMU:** PFUs and DFIs will submit vetted reports to the PMU quarterly and annually. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 82]  
- **PMU consolidation and feedback loop:** The PMU will review and integrate reports to ensure alignment with logical framework indicators and compliance with environmental and social safeguards and gender action plans, and will share feedback with DFIs/PFUs for continuous improvement. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 82]  

- **Gender-related monitoring and reporting responsibilities:** DFIs are responsible for ensuring project compliance with gender requirements and reporting on the Gender Action Plan (GAP) to the GFF during implementation. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 142]  
- **PMU review of DFI GAP reporting:** The PMU will conduct the initial DFIs’ GAP report review and subsequent improvement assessment in line with the facility launch process. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 142]  
- **Accredited Entity oversight and audit:** ADB (as Accredited Entity) will oversee the governance mechanism via the PMU, require quarterly reports on implementation (including gender-related progress against the approved GAP and other EAS/impact information), and will hire its own independent auditor to oversee this process. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 142]  

- **Planned strengthening (ITAP recommendation):** The Independent Technical Advisory Panel (ITAP) recommends an enhanced monitoring framework that provides early warning of market transformation indicators, including regular assessments of technology cost curves and market conditions, systematic review of portfolio alignment with pre-defined adjustment triggers, and periodic evaluation of concessionality requirements with pre-defined triggers for adjustment. [05_gcf-b42-02-add13-funding-proposal-package-fp271, p. 125]

FP270 describes implementation arrangements covering institutional roles/coordination, staffing and financial management, procurement, and contractor/sub-contractor execution modalities. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]

- **Institutional roles and coordination:** MOWRAM is responsible for overall project management, and the PMU is responsible for overall work plans and budgets, communications, coordination with the NDCDS PIU on agriculture support activities, and implementing social and environmental safeguards (among other tasks). [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]  
- **PMU leadership and reporting line:** The PMU will be led by IFAD and will report to the Ministry of Economy and Finance/General Department of Resettlement (GEF-DR) to guide the resettlement path. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]  
- **Component implementation responsibility:** NDCDS is responsible for implementation of Component 4, with close technical coordination between MIDWDRAM and NDCDS to ensure synergies between components. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]  
- **Provincial-level coordination:** The PMU will coordinate with NDCDS and other implementing agencies at the provincial level, and with service providers at the provincial level as required. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 44]  

- **Staffing setup:** MOWRAM is the lead project agency and NCCD is an implementing partner, and PMU and PPU will be set up for MOWRAM and NCCD with a combined team of 10 staff members to support implementation. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 110]  
- **Financial management (FM) arrangements:** The project’s FM function and internal controls are to be maintained by the Finance Units of MOWRAM and NCCD, which are described as having experience with internationally donor-funded projects. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 110]  
- **Contracted FM support:** Contract finance staff will be hired to support daily FM functions such as maintaining records, producing reports, submitting IFR and VAT returns on time, and preparing budgets for submission to IFAD. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 110]  

- **Procurement framework:** Procurement procedures are guided by the IFAD Procurement Manual, and the excerpt also situates procurement within Cambodia’s public procurement legal framework (Law on Public Procurement 2007 and related regulations/SOPs). [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 108]  
- **Procurement planning and controls:** A Project Procurement Arrangement Letter (PALL) will set detailed procurement requirements and thresholds (including IFAD prior review of contracts), and the NDCDS PIU will prepare an overall Project Implementation Plan and annual procurement plans aligned with AWPBS, requiring a PID “no objection” before procurement proceeds. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 109]  
- **Procurement monitoring tools:** The Project Implementation Plan (PIP) and Open Procurement Evaluation System (OPEN) will be used to prepare and monitor procurement implementation progress, and contracts will be registered and updated (quarterly) in the IFAD Contract Management Tool (CMT). [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 109]  

- **Fiduciary capacity and mitigation measures:** IFAD conducted FM and procurement assessments during design, concluding executing entities had capacity to meet IFAD standards, while also agreeing additional measures to enhance fiduciary capacity (e.g., self-certification forms, contractor prequalification, compliance screening). [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 103]  
- **Use of sub-contractors for ESCMP:** The ESCMP will be implemented with sub-contractors appointed by Provincial Project Implementation Units (PUIs), with contractors adhering to relevant FM rules and regulations, and with capacity support and consultants engaged to strengthen MOIVRAM PMJ and PDWRAM. [06_gcf-b42-02-add12-funding-proposal-package-fp270, p. 105]

### Description

176. There is a risk related to the timing for approval of CAISAR by the GCF Board which is expected to be undertaken in 2025. Delay in this approval could impact the plans of MOWRAM, the financing schedule of IFAD and AIBB and impose additional costs and impact the financial returns from the project.

### Mitigation Measure(s)

177. The NOA, IFAD and AIBB will try to expedite the process of design and approval to ensure that the FFP is submitted according to the required modules and will endeavour to address all comments received from GCF as efficiently as possible.

## Selected Risk Factor 2: Technical & Operational Capacity

| Category | Probability | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Technical and operational | Medium | Medium |

### While controls such as due diligence, sanctions screening, and continuous monitoring manage many risks associated with compliance, there are still inherent challenges in implementing these measures effectively. Considering these factors, the residual compliance risk rating for the project is medium. However, given the project’s intended safeguards and ongoing external vulnerabilities inherent in the operational environment, this rating may be revised.

## GCF portfolio concentration risk

### In the case of approval, the impact of this proposal on the GCF portfolio risk remains non-material and within the risk appetite in terms of concentration levels; results area, single proposal area of concentration.

It is recommended that the Board consider the above factors in its decision.
